meta.title: Qiskit Fall Fest Central Asia 2026
meta.description: The first Qiskit Fall Fest in Central Asia. Five Saturdays of quantum computing at Nazarbayev University, Astana. Free, 70–100 seats.
meta.cocDescription: The code of conduct for Qiskit Fall Fest Central Asia 2026.

hero.lede: Introducing future generations to the quantum frontier.

about.title: About the fest
body: Qiskit Fall Fest is an annual global initiative by IBM Quantum: student teams at leading universities around the world run lectures, workshops and hackathons on quantum computing.
In 2025 that meant more than 32,000 participants across 150 universities.
In 2026 the festival comes to Central Asia for the first time — to Nazarbayev University in Astana.

whatYouGet.title: What you get
items: Access to real IBM quantum computers through the IBM Quantum Platform
Four lectures from the ground up: linear algebra → Python → quantum mechanics → quantum computing
A hands-on practice session after every lecture
A hackathon with a defense in front of a jury
A certificate at one of two levels
Speakers at the intersections of quantum × medicine, finance, cryptography and AI
Merch and prizes from our partners

program.title: Program
program.subtitle: Read it as a quantum circuit — every week is a qubit, every session is a gate, and the hackathon is the measurement.

w1-lecture.title: Lecture: linear algebra for quantum computing
w1-lecture.description: Vectors, matrices, complex numbers and the Dirac notation — everything you need to read a quantum state. No prior background assumed.

w1-practice.title: Practice session
w1-practice.description: Working through the lecture material by hand and in code.

w2-lecture.title: Lecture: Python for quantum computing
w2-lecture.description: The Python you actually need for Qiskit — environment, notebooks, NumPy, plotting.

w2-practice.title: Practice session
w2-practice.description: Setting up your environment and running your first circuits.

w3-lecture.title: Lecture: quantum mechanics fundamentals
w3-lecture.description: Superposition, entanglement, and measurement — the physics behind the model.

w3-practice.title: Practice session
w3-practice.description: Simulating states and measurements in Qiskit.

w3-speaker.title: Guest speaker
w3-speaker.description: A talk at an intersection of quantum computing with another field. Speaker [ TBD ].

w4-lecture.title: Lecture: quantum computing with Qiskit
w4-lecture.description: Gates, circuits and algorithms — and running them on real IBM hardware.

w4-practice.title: Practice session
w4-practice.description: Building and submitting jobs to the IBM Quantum Platform.

w4-lab.title: Photonics laboratory
w4-lab.description: A hands-on session in the photonics lab — quantum phenomena on real optical equipment.

w4-activity.title: Activity
w4-activity.description: A team activity to warm up before the hackathon.

w5-hackathon.title: Hackathon and jury defense
w5-hackathon.description: Four base tasks plus one project task, teams of three, four to five hours of code, then a defense in front of the jury.

hackathon.title: Hackathon
hackathon.lede: The festival closes with a measurement: a full day of building, then a defense in front of a jury.
hackathon.format: Four base tasks plus one project task.
hackathon.timing: Four to five hours of code, then a defense.

certificates.title: Certificates
certificates.lede: Two levels, both issued after the festival.
certificates.excellenceBody: At least four lectures attended, plus participation in the hackathon.
certificates.completionBody: At least three lectures attended, plus participation in the hackathon.

items.q: I'm still in school — can I join?
items.a: Yes. The lectures start from the ground up and assume no university coursework. If you can follow along and you're curious, you belong here.

items.q: Do I need a background in physics?
items.a: No. Week 3 covers the quantum mechanics you need, and weeks 1 and 2 build the linear algebra and Python underneath it.

items.q: Do I need to know how to program?
items.a: A basic level helps, but week 2 is dedicated to the Python you actually need for Qiskit. You do need to bring a laptop.

items.q: Can I come to only some of the Saturdays?
items.a: You can. Keep in mind that a certificate of completion requires at least three lectures, and a certificate with excellence requires at least four — both plus the hackathon.
Not to attend the festival. It is required for either certificate, and it is the part most people remember.

coc.title: Code of Conduct
coc.lede: Qiskit Fall Fest Central Asia 2026 is a learning space. Everyone is welcome, and everyone is responsible for keeping it that way.

sections.heading: What we expect
sections.body: Treat every participant, speaker, organizer and member of staff with respect. Assume good faith. Ask before you take someone's photo. Give people room to ask beginner questions — most of the room is a beginner at something.

sections.heading: What is not acceptable
sections.body: Harassment in any form, including comments about gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, religion or level of experience. Intimidation, stalking, unwelcome photography, sustained disruption of talks, and unwelcome physical contact or attention.

sections.heading: Academic honesty
sections.body: The hackathon is judged on what your team built. Use of libraries, published work and AI tools is fine when you say so. Passing off someone else's work as your own is not.

sections.heading: Consequences
sections.body: Organizers may take any action they consider appropriate, from a warning to removal from the event without a refund of any travel or costs, and exclusion from future events.

sections.heading: Reporting
sections.body: If you experience or witness a breach of this code, contact any organizer on site, or write to us. Reports are handled confidentially.
